question.problem:
Find ${lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{+}}f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{-}}f(x)$ for the function given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}+1 & \text{ for }\,x\le 0 \\ \sqrt{x}+2 & \text{ for }\,x\ge 1\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Approaching $x=0$ from the left, we have $x<0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={e}^{x}+1.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}({e}^{x}+1) \\  & ={e}^{0}+1 \\  & =1+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The right-sided limit ${lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x)$ does not exist since $f(x)$ is not defined on the interval $x\in (0,1).$ 

Consequently, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x)=2,\,{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$
